about.text: Lactoferrin (LF), also known as lactotransferrin (LTF), is a multifunctional protein found in milk and mucus which is encoded by the LTF gene in humans. It functions as an antimicrobial protein and affects the body's immune response in a complex way, with both pro- and anti-inflammatory effects.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.

how.text: Lactoferrin is a small fraction of milk protein, so it is fished out of the flow with a cation-exchange column and eluted with salt. Membrane filtration and salt extraction are also used.
